data.long_meaning: Akhlaak refers to moral virtues, good conduct, and ethical behavior. It is derived from the Arabic root word 'kh-l-k', which means 'to make smooth, to perfect'. The name conveys the idea of cultivating good character and living a righteous life. The name Akhlaak carries the meaning “Moral virtues, good conduct” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Akhlaak usually hope their child will grow to embody moral virtues, good conduct and live with faith, good character and purpose.
